A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thrombolytic treatment of acute myocardial infraction was not a success in the late 1970s because of the lack of a large number (i.e. 1000 or more) of patients treated in a randomized fashion.
thrombolytic therapies in AMI have been a great success.

the Italian SK trial was the first to be carried out in CCUs and to show that thrombolytic treatment did not reduce the mortality in AMI; and that GISSI-2 [5] and -3 [6] were two landmark studies that showed that thrombolysis was the most effective treatment of AMI.
